scenario: A world-sailing academy admits trainees if they have either elite navigation skill or elite sail-trim skill. A 10% wildcard also admits people with neither trait. Coaches think the two skills are negatively related among admitted sailors.

data.description: Selection is based on either trait plus a wildcard.

question: Among admitted sailors, compute (a) P(navigation | sail-trim, selected), and (b) P(navigation | not sail-trim, selected). Is the negative association real or a selection artifact?

ground_truth.explanation: The apparent negative relationship is caused by selecting on either strength.

naive_answer: Navigation and sail-trim skill look negatively related among admitted sailors, so the skills must trade off.
naive_trap: This is collider bias from the admission rule.
